title: The antisymmetric cubical line has a multiplicative frame extension
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral Noetherian affine scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], where Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact, and normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. A commutative $S$-group scheme has addition, inverse and identity as $S$-morphisms satisfying the commutative group identities [def-sc-group-scheme, def-pc-fibre-product]; separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $p:H\to S$ be a commutative $S$-group scheme, with addition $m:H\times_SH\to H$, identity $e:S\to H$ and projections $p_1,p_2:H\times_SH\to H$, which is smooth separated and of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with semiabelian geometric fibres [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres], and write $\iota=[-1]_H$. For a supplied cubical rigidified line $(L,r,\tau)$ [def-sfb-cubical-rigidified-line], put $D=L\otimes(\iota^*L)^\vee$, where the dual is $\mathcal Hom(-,\mathcal O_H)$ [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Form the actual frame torsor $q:E=D^\times\to H$: for $h:U\to H$, its sections over $h$ are the isomorphisms $\mathcal O_U\simeq h^*D$. Scalar multiplication defines its $\mathbf G_{m,S}$-action, where $\mathbf G_{m,S}=\operatorname{Spec}_S\mathcal O_S[t,t^{-1}]$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. There is a commutative $S$-group structure on $E$, whose identity is the frame of $e^*D$ induced by $r$, making $1\to\mathbf G_{m,S}\to E\xrightarrow{q}H\to1$ exact as fppf sheaves [def-pc-fppf-site]. Its multiplication is induced by the isomorphism $p_1^*D\otimes p_2^*D\simeq m^*D$ obtained by pulling $\tau$ back along $(x,y)\mapsto(x,y,-x-y)$. This isomorphism satisfies the associative, commutative and unit identities as sheaf maps, not just on geometric points. The scheme $E$ is smooth separated and of finite presentation over $S$ with semiabelian geometric fibres. The morphism $q$ is affine, faithfully flat and of finite presentation; its group-kernel action equals the frame-scaling action. The tautological frame gives $q^*D\simeq\mathcal O_E$. No ampleness assumption or conclusion is made.

source.place: I, cubical torsors and associated extensions (especially the cube/second-difference calculus in I 2 and I 5). Agent-formulated antisymmetric-frame construction; local original WANTED, not a claimed verbatim numbered theorem. The multiplication is obtained from the cube at (x,y,-x-y).

proof.text: The dual of a line is a line: on a frame its evaluation pairing is ordinary multiplication. Thus the pullback/tensor identifications of lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor make $D=L\otimes(\iota^*L)^\vee$ invertible. The rigidification $r$ identifies $e^*D=e^*L\otimes(e^*L)^\vee$ with $\mathcal O_S$; denote its inverse frame by $u$. All subsequent cancellations use evaluation of a line against its dual, and so are canonical sheaf isomorphisms.

source.place: I §2 and I §5, local original WANTED; agent tensor calculation for the supplied rigidified line

proof.text:
Pull the supplied cube section back by $a(x,y)=(x,y,-x-y)$. The eight factors give
$$a^*\Theta_3(L)=\frac{L_0L_xL_yL_{-x-y}}{L_{x+y}L_{-y}L_{-x}L_0}=D_x\otimes D_y\otimes D_{x+y}^{\vee}.$$
The section $a^*\tau$ therefore defines $\mu:D_x\otimes D_y\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{x+y}$: explicitly $\mu$ is the unique map sending this section of $\operatorname{Hom}(D_{x+y},D_x\otimes D_y)$ to the identity after composition. Permutation invariance of $\tau$ gives $\mu_{x,y}=\mu_{y,x}$ through tensor symmetry. On either identity axis, the cube normalization and $r$ give $\mu(u\otimes v)=v=\mu(v\otimes u)$. These computations are pullbacks and evaluations of module sheaves, hence hold over every test scheme, including nonreduced ones.

source.place: I §2, supplied cube restricted to (x,y,-x-y); agent eight-factor cancellation, not a claimed numbered theorem

proof.text:
The geometric fibres inherit smoothness by lem-pc-proper-base-change, separatedness by lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change and finite type by lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change. They are connected: apply lem-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-power-integrality with $n=1$ to each semiabelian presentation. For a point $s\in S$ and an algebraic closure $\bar\kappa$ of $\kappa(s)$, the base change of the fibre $H_{\kappa(s)}$ to $\bar\kappa$ is such a geometric fibre, hence connected, so lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure makes every fibre of $p$ geometrically connected, as the factorization lemma requires. The base $S$ is reduced since each of its local rings is a domain. Compare the two isomorphisms from $D_x\otimes D_y\otimes D_z$ to $D_{x+y+z}$,
$$\mu_{x+y,z}(\mu_{x,y}\otimes1),\qquad \mu_{x,y+z}(1\otimes\mu_{y,z}).$$
Their ratio is a global unit $c$ on $H^3$: an automorphism of a line is multiplication by a unit, as is checked in local frames. On each coordinate axis, both composites reduce to the identity by the unit identities from step 2, so $c=1$ on all three axes. Apply lem-sfb-relative-group-unit-axis-factorization with $G=H$, $n=3$ and its reduced-base alternative. It gives $c=1$ as a regular function on $H^3$. Consequently $\mu$ is associative as a sheaf map.

source.place: Proposition 12.48, identity (79), and Remark 12.50, pp.246–247; agent application of the recorded relative unit-factorization theorem

proof.text:
Choose a Zariski open cover $(V_i)$ of $H$ by affine schemes carrying frames $d_i$ of $D$. On overlaps write $d_j=g_{ij}d_i$. The charts $V_i\times\mathbf G_m$ glue by $z_i=g_{ij}z_j$, since $g_{ik}=g_{ij}g_{jk}$. Lemma lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes supplies the glued scheme $E$. Its maps over $h:U\to H$ are exactly the frames $z_i h^*d_i$, which agree under these transitions. This identifies it with the actual frame functor in the statement. Apply lem-sfb-frame-product-laurent-algebra with base $H$, one line $D$, and $r=1$. It gives that $q$ is affine and the chart formula
$$q^{-1}(V_i)=\operatorname{Spec}R_i[z_i,z_i^{-1}]\quad(V_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i).$$

Define the product of frames $v:\mathcal O_U\simeq x^*D$ and $w:\mathcal O_U\simeq y^*D$ by $v\star w=\mu_{x,y}(v\otimes w)$, over $x+y$. This is natural in $U$, so Yoneda represents it by a scheme morphism $E\times_SE\to E$. The frame $u$ gives its identity section. For a frame $v$ over $x$, the perfect pairing $\mu_{x,-x}:D_x\otimes D_{-x}\simeq D_0$ has a unique frame $v^{-1}$ over $-x$ satisfying $\mu(v\otimes v^{-1})=u$; in local frames it is a unit times $z^{-1}$, and the uniqueness makes it natural and independent of frames. Yoneda therefore represents inversion too. The identities in steps 2–3 give the group identities on all generalized points, so Yoneda gives the commutative group identities as scheme morphisms. The projection $q$ respects addition and identity by construction.

source.place: I §2, cubical torsors and associated extensions; original WANTED, agent construction from the explicit multiplicative line

proof.text: The fibre at $e$ consists precisely of the frames $au$ with $a\in\mathbf G_m$, naturally over any $S$-scheme. Thus $j:a\mapsto au$ identifies $\mathbf G_m$ with the scheme-theoretic kernel. By the unit identities and bilinearity of $\mu$, $(au)\star v=av$; this is exactly frame scaling. Every $h:U\to H$ lifts to $E$ on a Zariski trivializing cover of $h^*D$. Such a cover is fppf by lem-pc-zariski-coverings-are-fppf, so $q$ is an epimorphism of fppf sheaves. Together with the computed kernel this proves the asserted exact sequence. It also identifies $(v,a)\mapsto(v,av)$ with $E\times_S\mathbf G_m\simeq E\times_HE$: for two frames of the same line their ratio is a unique unit.

source.place: I, multiplicative torsor construction; agent computation of the kernel, torsor action and local surjectivity

proof.text: On each affine frame chart, $q$ is the complement $z\ne0$ in $\mathbf A^1_{V_i}\to V_i$, hence smooth by sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth and lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes. Part (b) of the latter reads this as smoothness of the composite to $H$; lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source now makes $q$ smooth. Hence $q$ is flat by lem-pc-smooth-flat. It is surjective, since each chart has the section $z=1$. Its affine coordinate presentation $R_i[z,w]/(zw-1)$ makes it locally of finite presentation on this target cover, hence globally by lem-sfb-separated-lfp-target-open-locality. Affineness gives quasi-compactness and separatedness, hence quasi-separatedness, by lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence. Thus $q$ is faithfully flat and of finite presentation.

source.place: Frame Laurent charts of Tags 01M2 and 01LX; smooth open restriction and finite-presentation definitions as in the cited nodes

proof.text: Since $p:H\to S$ is smooth, lem-trf-smooth-composition applied to $q$ and $p$ shows that $E\to S$ is smooth. Both $q$ and $p$ are separated and of finite presentation. Apply the scheme case of lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition to conclude that $E\to S$ is separated and of finite presentation.

source.place: Frame construction; general composition properties of the morphisms, precisely the statements of the cited nodes

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $s:\operatorname{Spec}F\to S$. Choose its supplied presentation $1\to T=\mathbf G_{m,F}^r\to H_s\to A\to1$. Set $K=E_s\times_{H_s}T$. It is affine by the base-change and affine-target clauses of lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence. The formation of frames commutes with base change by their functorial definition. Its morphism to $T$ is the frame torsor of $D|_T$; the chart argument of step 7 works unchanged over $T$. Thus $K\to T$ is smooth of finite type; as $T=D_F(\mathbf Z^r)$ is smooth of finite type over $F$ by lem-sfb-diagonalizable-group-geometric-criteria, lem-trf-smooth-composition and the composition clause of lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change make $K$ smooth of finite type over $F$. Also $K\to T$ is flat and surjective with kernel $\mathbf G_m$. The affine flatness comparison and flat-surjective criterion give faithful flatness on coordinate rings. The kernel and quotient are connected by lem-sfb-diagonalizable-group-geometric-criteria, so lem-sfb-connected-group-extension makes $K$ connected. They are of multiplicative type, hence lem-sfb-commutative-multiplicative-type-extension makes the commutative $K$ isomorphic to $D_F(M)$ for a finitely generated $M$. A surjection $\mathbf Z^n\to M$ induces a surjection $F[\mathbf Z^n]\to F[M]$ compatible with comultiplication, so $K$ is a closed subgroup scheme of $\mathbf G_m^n$, i.e. of multiplicative type in the sense of lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-largest-subtorus. The smooth-connected clause of lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-largest-subtorus now makes $K$ a torus, split over algebraically closed $F$. The composite $E_s\to A$ is fppf locally surjective: lift first to $H_s$ and then to its frame torsor, refining the covers (the second lift is Zariski local, hence fppf). Its scheme kernel is $K$ by the fibre-product definition. Therefore $1\to K\to E_s\to A\to1$ is a semiabelian presentation of $E_s$. This includes $r=0$.

source.place: Corollary 12.22, p.239, and torus criteria in §12; agent application to the inverse image of the supplied torus, using the cited exact connectedness statement

proof.text: At the universal generalized point $q:E\to H$, the representing frame functor gives its tautological frame $\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{\sim}q^*D$. Its inverse is the required trivialization $q^*D\simeq\mathcal O_E$. On $q^{-1}V_i$ this frame is $z_iq^*d_i$, and the transition identity in step 4 shows the frames agree on overlaps. No positivity assertion has been used.
